title: Absa Launches New Digital Platform Targeting Kenyan Customers
desc: Absa Bank Kenya has launched Absa Next, a digital platform combining banking, savings, investments and loans in one application.
content:
Absa Bank Kenya has launched Absa Next, a new digital financial platform that brings banking, savings, investments and lending services together in one application.

The platform was launched in Kenya on Friday, September 25, as the bank expands its digital services and seeks to attract customers who increasingly manage their finances through mobile devices. Today's reports say Absa Next is available to both existing Absa customers and people who do not currently bank with Absa.

Unlike a conventional banking application focused mainly on account management and transactions, Absa Next is designed as a broader digital finance platform. Its services include savings, borrowing and other financial products, with lifestyle-related features also incorporated into the platform.

The platform's launch follows work Absa had already undertaken to develop a digital-only proposition for the next generation of customers. Absa's 2025 integrated report said the first phase of Absa Next had been completed in pilot, with market rollout planned for 2026.

Today's launch therefore represents the move from that development phase into wider market availability.

For customers, one of the notable features is that access is not restricted to people who already hold an Absa account. Reports on the launch indicate that Kenyan users can access the platform using a Kenyan identification document, widening its potential customer base.

The platform also includes digital savings and lending options. Today's reports indicate that eligible users can access loans of up to KSh1 million, although the amount available to an individual customer will depend on the applicable assessment and product conditions.

The launch comes as Kenyan banks continue investing in mobile and digital channels as customers increasingly expect faster access to financial services without having to visit branches.

Absa's wider technology strategy has also focused on speeding up customer onboarding, credit decisions and digital service delivery. The group reported in August that its technology investments were being used to simplify banking and expand digital lending across its African operations.

For Kenyan consumers, Absa Next adds another digital option for managing financial services from a mobile device. Its impact will ultimately depend on how customers adopt the platform, the pricing of its products and the terms attached to its savings and lending services.

The launch also intensifies competition among financial institutions seeking to serve Kenya's increasingly mobile-first banking market.
